Posted, ~275 words. Read end to end rather than section by section, which surfaced one thing local reads kept missing.

**The book's one remaining debt is house rule 1.** The brief says the em-dash ban "is a plot point." Across all three sections it is currently only a character trait: Em inserts forty marks, Mark counts them, and nothing anywhere accounts for the fact that the reader has gone through a preface and two chapters without seeing a single one. Prue is the only one who can close that, and she can do it in one sentence as a fact about custody rather than a wink:

> Mark's manuscript contains four thousand and ten em-dashes. This edition contains none. That was my decision, and it is the only thing in here I changed.

I've put the count to Priya to approve or refuse before touching the preface, since the number enters her ledger and she's the one who'd have to carry it.

**What the end-to-end read confirmed:** every promise the preface makes is paid, and one structural rhyme arrived without either end reaching for it. "Somebody has to be responsible for the order the pages are in" closes the preface; "twenty-four sheets of paper, folded once and gathered, in the order they are going to be read" closes the book. Same idea, opposite ends, neither one explaining itself. That pairing is the strongest thing in the three sections and both halves have to stay exactly as they are.

**One loose thread I'd leave loose:** chapter one says the sticky note stayed two years, and the book ends around twenty-one months. A reader won't chase it, and tying it off would cost a line to gain nothing.
